provenance.notes: Related entry: this is a different exponent draw of the same template as our codes/996-166-32.json (same irregular 5x12 "pair-complement-2" template, class 0, same lift Z_83); its pairing differs from that entry's in 3 of the 25 X-row/Z-row cells and all 80 exponents are a new random draw, so the check matrices differ, and its lightest logical found is 34 instead of 32. Our contribution: the irregular 5x12 "pair-complement-2" base template on which the pair-partition rule is applied (the 12 block columns form 6 column pairs; each of the 5 block rows contains all pairs but two, so every check has weight 8; the left-out pairs form a triangle and a path on the 6 pairs, so two pairs have qubit degree 4 and the rest degree 3; the same template on both sides; design rate 1/6); the census of this family (259 X/Z classes up to symmetry, ranked by a permanent-vector upper bound, our generalisation of App. A of arXiv:2609.30069 to sparse templates); the symmetric couple solver and its overnight extension that found this pairing (solution 115 of a pool of class-0 solutions grown by symmetric depth-first restarts and an exact large-neighbourhood search); the lift P = 83 and this exponent draw; and the distance screening described in notes/996-166-34.md. Construction framework, not ours: the pair-partition construction and its paired-difference equations on CPM exponents are Okada and Kasai's (arXiv:2607.14091), where they are applied to complete J x L templates; the design-rate count R = 1 - J_tot/L_stab and the permanent-vector bound (App. A of arXiv:2609.30069) are from Lee, Okada, Maskara, Kasai and Zhou (arXiv:2609.30069), whose outlook names quantum-compatible irregular templates as a natural direction. Quasi-cyclic CSS LDPC codes from circulant permutation matrices go back to Hagiwara and Imai (arXiv:quant-ph/0701020), and CSS pairs of two irregular LDPC codes were analysed by Hagiwara and Imai (arXiv:0801.1361). Board precedents of the same commutation rule at weight 8 on the complete (3,8) template include codes/912-234-22.json by @jacksongquera, codes/904-230-22.json by @vprusso (which also cites the lifted-product construction of Panteleev and Kalachev, arXiv:2111.03654) and the published codes/584-150-18.json (Okada-Kasai); our codes/990-198-17.json applies the rule to a different irregular template with weight-7 checks, our codes/1000-200-29.json to the 4x10 "pair-complement" template (all pairs but one) at rate 1/5, and our codes/996-166-32.json to this template. In our check for codes/990-198-17.json (2026-10-22: arXiv:2607.14091, arXiv:2609.30069, the Okada-Kasai project page, web searches) we did not find a pair-partition code on an irregular template; literature novelty is not claimed. Distance: a witness-backed upper bound (confidence upper_bound), d <= 34 on both sides; no lower bound is claimed. Stern information-set decoding found a weight-34 X logical (one 1200 s run) and, on the Z side, weight-36 logicals at lightest, and nothing lighter, in 8 recorded runs per side (3 x 300 s, 3 x 1200 s, 2 x 1 h; about 520000 iterations in each 1 h run) plus the 3 s and 60 s screens; per-run results ranged from 34 to 52 (X) and 36 to 46 (Z), so the search had not settled and a lighter logical may exist. The code has an X<->Z symmetry: a qubit permutation (found with nauty, re-checked row by row) carries the X checks onto the Z checks and back, so d_X = d_Z, and the filed Z witness is the image of the weight-34 X witness. The board's verify/heuristic_distance.py (RIS, orbit pass over 1 symmetry partition, 400000 gf2_fast trials, seed 3) returned 'inconclusive': its lightest logicals had weight 80 (X) and 102 (Z), so at this size it did not get down to the claimed 34 and found nothing lighter. At the same Stern ladder (3 x 1200 s and 2 x 1 h per side), 8 of the 10 deep runs on codes/996-166-32.json reached 32; this code's 10 stayed at 34 or above. Dedup: the trusted gate flags a shared WL signature with codes/996-166-32.json; the board's research/audits/permutation_audit.py returns 'undecided' (equal ranks and X/Z row-space intersection dimension; typed Tanner graphs not isomorphic under nauty, with or without an X/Z swap; row spaces too large to enumerate). Checked, not equivalent: in each of the four row spaces the vectors of weight <= 9 are exactly the 415 weight-8 checks (complete Brouwer-Zimmermann enumeration), so by Leon's minimum-weight argument any equivalence, with or without an X/Z swap, would be a coloured Tanner-graph isomorphism, and the nauty canonical forms differ. Proof in notes/996-166-34.md.
